mentl/04fdd26:
The banked probe ran and its first job was killing a claim the entry had
just made without measuring it — that mn-open-row-second-field takes the
same bind mn-findtag takes. It does not. On the shipping rule the counting
eprint reads xa=0 xb=0 for findtag and xa=1 xb=1 for the second-field
micro: same writer, same two row handles, different inputs. One side knows
{handle}, the other {region_id}, and each carries the other's field across,
so the full set really is {handle, region_id} and region_id really sits at
offset 4. The control passes for a reason. findtag passes because handle
sorts first in both the partial set and the true one.

The floor built last iteration did its job. With the open-open bind
recording nothing, both micros trap in main at one named floor —
`field 'handle' on { handle: Int | r25043@e1 }` and
`field 'region_id' on { handle: Int | r25043@e1 }` — enclosing fn read off
the emit, not assumed. The known set in the second is {handle}, not
{region_id}, so main's receiver learns handle through pick's scheme and
everything else from that single bind.

That reframes the arc. unify_two_open_records records the union of what
both sides know, so deleting it or free-tailing it discards a fact the
graph had proved — which is why the flip broke a correct program instead
of merely refusing an incorrect one. The defect is the second half of the
same write, the assertion that nothing further exists, and the two halves
have to be separated rather than removed together.

mentl/04bacc6:
subst_row's EtVar arm returned the empty row when the var was solved to
a closed row, discarding the bound row's whole present set at
instantiation — every caller of every declared-row fn read a bare row,
and no effect instance ever crossed a fn boundary. The merge arm reads
the binding live, freshened through the same mapping the params use,
under the solved tail. free_in_row and occurs_in_row complete the trio:
both descend a bound tail exactly as subst_row now traverses it —
collection without descent left the inner payload vars unquantified and
shared raw across call sites, so map's install bound the shared answer
var and every later handler decl collided against it.

With the root: publish_with_instances keeps a declared-bare name's
parameterized instance at publish; inf_add_row_unified joins same-named
instance fragments by position, gated on the install frame (a tee body
is one install's scope; a caller's independent callee instances never
join); the effects.mn name-set seams upgrade bare to parameterized;
prelude declares iterate_from before iterate (callee-first kills the
pre-scheme row bake); chase_deep canonicalizes free leaves to roots and
chase_row_deep covers EAType payloads and TCont worlds; the compare
leaf stashes its f64 pair (the bare f64.lt select never assembled);
spec_pairs_walk chases body-bound vars.

mentl/043efe0:
codegen.lux: FnStmt and LambdaExpr proto construction now includes
handler_tables when the function body contains handle expressions.
Previously the tables were compiled into the child context but dropped
when building the proto tuple (8 fields instead of 9). This caused
"invalid handler table index: 0" for functions like fibonacci_via_effects
that return handle expressions. wasm_ultimate.lux now prints fib(10)=55.

vm.rs: Register str_slice as a Rust VM builtin (delegates to the same
logic as string_slice). Needed because prelude.lux now uses str_slice
for string operations to avoid HM type contamination with the list-only
slice function. Also relaxes the FnProto tuple guard from <=8 to <=9
to accept handler_tables as the 9th field.

sonido/0401d50:
Move hardware knob mapping infrastructure from sonido-core/sonido-daisy to
sonido-platform where it belongs — noon presets and biased ADC conversion are
hardware UX concerns, not platform-agnostic DSP primitives.

Three new modules in sonido-platform:
- param_map: scale-aware ADC→parameter conversion (moved from sonido-daisy)
- noon: guitarist sweet-spot values per effect (moved from sonido-core)
- knob_mapping: Hothouse 6-knob→param-index maps + knob_to_param() convenience

New EffectSlot in sonido-daisy consolidates the shared pattern across binaries:
bypass crossfade (5ms SmoothedParam ramp), NaN/Inf sanitization, and noon-biased
knob mapping in one struct. single_effect uses it directly (213→172 lines).
sonido_pedal uses the standalone utilities (BypassCrossfade, sanitize_stereo,
CONTROL_POLL_EVERY) alongside its DAG-based graph processing.

two-top/041bcb5:
Builds the soak harness on top of Phase 5's checksum pipeline. Each seed
is a complete reproduction recipe: fuzz_replay(seed) deterministically
generates 1800 frames of inputs (Xoshiro256**), and fuzz_one(seed) runs
the replay through compute_checksum_tsv with SyncTest panics caught.

Per the leaner shape decided up-front:
  * No auto-issue creation. Failed Actions notifications cover signal.
  * No auto-commit to main. Operator triages artifacts and commits real
    regressions to tests/demos/regressions/ with context.
  * Workflow uploads divergent seeds' .bmrg + .log as a single artifact
    with 30-day retention. Seed alone is enough to reproduce locally.

CLI updates (crates/replay_sync/src/main.rs):
  * --fuzz <seed> input source, mutually exclusive with --demo.
  * --emit-bmrg <path> writes the loaded-or-generated replay before
    running, so the workflow's artifact is the exact bytes the fuzzer
    saw. Round-trip verified locally: --fuzz <seed> ≡ --demo <emitted>.
  * --fuzz path catches SyncTest panics via run_replay_caught so the
    workflow's bash loop sees a clean non-zero exit.

Library (crates/replay_sync/src/fuzz.rs):
  * fuzz_replay(seed) — deterministic 1800-frame replay generator.
    Inputs respect wire format: stick clamped to -127..=127, reserved
    button bits 4-7 forced to zero.
  * run_replay_caught(replay) — pipeline runner with catch_unwind.
  * fuzz_one(seed) — convenience wrapping the two.
  * FuzzError enum with Display + std::error::Error.

Tests (crates/replay_sync/tests/fuzz.rs):
  * Same seed → identical replay; different seeds → different.
  * Frame count and wire-constraint invariants.
  * fuzz_one(0xC0DEBEEF) returns Ok (default known-good seed).

Workflow (.github/workflows/fuzz_soak.yml):
  * Nightly cron 04:00 UTC + workflow_dispatch with seed_count and
    base_seed inputs (validated as unsigned integers via env-var
    indirection to defang any injection vector).
  * Single ubuntu-latest job, Swatinem/rust-cache, release
